title: Record the audio: the recorder is ready

The sheet has 2,849 takes: A1 first (takes 1–980: 945 new, 19 replacing the synthetic voice, 16 re-takes), then A2 (1,869). About 100 takes a session, roughly 30 minutes; A1 is about 10 sessions. After each session press Export new and tell me; the full one-page guide is below. detail:
*Executor, 2026-10-19. The sheet: `recorder_A2.html` at the repo root. Its list: `a2_build/recording_list.csv`. Both come from `python3 build_recorder.py A2`.*

## What is on the sheet
The sheet lists every take that the current deck still needs: **2,849 takes**. The A1 subdeck comes first, then A2, each in study order (`study_order.csv`, study order v3; same order as `a2_build/study_order/recording_order_v3.csv`).

| | takes | of which |
|---|---|---|
| **A1** (takes 1–980) | **980** | 945 new · 19 replace the synthetic voice · 16 re-takes |
| **A2** (takes 981–2,849) | **1,869** | 1,795 new · 74 replace the synthetic voice |
| kinds | | 1,813 words · 981 example sentences (`<id>_s`) · 55 sentence cards (`S-####`) |

These takes are not on the sheet:
- the 415 base-deck cards and 150 A2-list cards whose July takes still match the card;
- the 31 B1-deferred rows and the 4 merged-away keys.

**Re-takes (16, all A1; a red "re-take" badge shows the old words):**
- The words are now wrong, so the old take has been withdrawn and the card is silent until you re-record it:
  - 265 *lūpos* (was *lūpa*);
  - 249 *mobilusis telefonas · mobiliojo telefono* (the old genitive was wrong);
  - A2-0033 *rugsėjis · rugsėjo* (was *rugsėjio*);
  - A2-0104 *čekis* (was *kvitas*);
  - A2-0902 *Prašom pakartoti*;
  - A2-0903 *Prašom užrašyti*.
- The ten colours (069–078) said the genitive (*raudonas · raudono*). The card now shows the feminine (*raudonas · raudona*). The old takes are correct Lithuanian and stay in the deck until you replace them.

The other wording changes were never recorded, so they appear as ordinary new takes in their new wording: A2-0375 *Prašom kalbėti lėčiau*, A2-1166 *Prašom sėstis*, A2-0964 *…parekomenduoti?*, A2-1674_s, A2-1713_s.

## How to record
1. **On the Mac**, open this file in **Chrome**: `~/Library/CloudStorage/ProtonDrive-…/50-59 Languages & Learning Method/51 Lithuanian Language & Culture/51.04 Lithuanian Flashcard Project/recorder_A2.html`. You can double-click it in Finder and choose *Open With → Google Chrome*. Use the same browser every time, because your takes are kept in that browser's storage. Safari and Firefox are untested for local files.
2. Click **Enable microphone & start**. The sheet jumps to the first take that has not been recorded yet.
3. Read everything in the dashed box: the headword, then its forms, one breath apart. The *italic* line under the word is the stressed form; say it that way. For sentences, read the sentence once, naturally.
4. Press **Space** to start. Wait for "SPEAK NOW" (0.4 s), speak, then press **Space** again. With auto-advance on, the sheet moves to the next take. **P** plays the take back; **←/→** move between takes.

**Phone:** opening the file on a phone does not work, because the microphone and the stored takes need a web address. Record on the Mac.

**Session size:** about **100 takes**, roughly 30 minutes at ~15 s a take. The A1 share is about 4 hours in all, so about 10 sessions. Stop when your voice tires; the sheet resumes where you left off.

## After each session: Export new
- Click **⬇ Export new takes**. You get one ZIP with only the takes recorded since the last export (`lt_A2_takes_<date>_batch.zip`). Batches add up; a re-recorded take goes out again in the next batch.
- **Put the ZIP in** `a2_build/audio/inbox/` in the project folder. ZIPs there are not committed to git. Then tell the executor: "audio batch in the inbox".
- **Export all** is the safety copy. It holds every take in the browser, plus older clips the sheet has set aside (`superseded/`, `off_list/`). Use it once at the end, or before clearing the browser.

## What happens next (executor)
1. The executor converts each clip to the `dest` path in `recording_list.csv` (`audio/` for the 520-word base, `audio_a2/` for the rest) and writes the key's row in `audio_source.tsv`, including what was said.
2. When the sheet is regenerated, recorded takes drop off it. The browser storage name stays fixed (`lt_recorder_A2_afb2ebe2`), so regenerating never loses a take.
3. If a card's words change later, its stored take is set aside, not deleted, and the card comes back as a re-take.

title: AnkiWeb description and the five choices in it
ask: The text is below with the final counts. Decide: (1) sign it with your name, or keep "the author"; (2) the share title; (3) the tags; (4) replace the old v2.0 share, or keep both; (5) licence CC BY-NC 4.0, as in the repo's LICENSE. Write your choices in the note.
options: Approve with the changes in my note
detail:
### The text

**Lietuvių Flashcards — A1 (v3.0)**

Lithuanian from zero to A1 through pictures, phrases and sentences. The first of two subdecks; A2 follows as a separate package.

**What is in the deck**

1,186 cards, ordered by usefulness: survival words and everyday phrases come first.

- 685 picture cards for words
- 135 phrase cards (greetings, thanks, asking for things)
- 331 cloze cards for function words and forms
- 35 sentence cards with a picture

**How a card works**

The front shows a picture with an English caption in the band below it. The back gives the Lithuanian word with its stress mark, gender and forms (genitive, present and past, or the feminine), and the English gloss. Phrase cards add a note on when to use the phrase. Cloze cards show a Lithuanian sentence with a blank and the English as a hint; sentence cards pair the blank with a picture.

Stress marks are taken from Wiktionary, kirtis.info and the LKŽ, never guessed.

**The pictures**

The art is an original house style: a civil-defence training manual from a free Lithuania of 1981. The pictures are AI-generated in that style and reviewed by hand. A few cards show real interwar places and people: the Lituanica with Darius and Girėnas, Basanavičius as the doctor, Čiurlionis as the artist, with a painting after one of his public-domain works on the easel.

**Audio**

547 cards carry recordings by the author, a native speaker, reading the word and its forms. 19 older cards still use a synthetic voice, and the other 620 are silent until the next update.

Fonts: Brygada 1918 (SIL Open Font Licence), embedded. In night mode, leave image inversion off.

**Upgrading from an earlier version**

The note types changed in v3.0. Delete the old deck before importing this one; study history from older versions does not carry over. From v3.0 onward the card IDs are stable, so future updates import in place and keep your progress.

**Licence and credits**

CC BY-NC 4.0: share and adapt for non-commercial use, with credit and a link to the source. Word list from the Fluent Forever 625, extended from A1 English word lists. Pictures, data and recordings by the author.

Source and issues: https://github.com/dainius-sileika/Lithuanian_Flashcards

### The choices, with background

1. **Licence wording.** The repo `LICENSE` is CC BY-NC 4.0 (not BY-NC-SA) and names the owner in the required attribution string. The text follows it. If a different licence is wanted for the published deck, change `LICENSE` first, then this line.
2. **Signing the description.** The rule "name no living person" was applied to the owner too: the text says "the author" and leaves the credit to the GitHub link and `LICENSE`. Decide whether to sign it with a name.
3. **Audio sentence.** The brief said "the 520 core cards have native-speaker recordings"; the data says otherwise. `audio_source.tsv` marks 427 recordings as human and 93 as `azure-neural` (the files differ: 48 kbps, no ID3 tag). On 2026-10-19, of the 446 base cards in the A1 block, 427 were human, 18 synthetic, 1 without audio (`531_batonas`); the 75 base rows with `level = A2` are exactly the 75 remaining synthetic ones. If the 18 were re-recorded without updating the ledger, correct the ledger first. The retag for order v3 may move some of these between subdecks; recount from the manifest.
4. **Historical cards left out on purpose.** Gustaitis (A2-0782), the 1939 basketball team (138 komanda, `level = A2`; A2-1297) and the two posters (*Velnio nuotaka* on A2-1191, *Milžino paunksmė* on A2-1360) are A2-level rows and not in this package. They belong in the A2 description. 097 prezidentas and 123 autorius ship without likenesses. If order v3 retags any of them A1, add them to "The pictures".
5. **Title** for the AnkiWeb share, e.g. "Lietuvių Flashcards — Lithuanian A1 (pictures, audio, stress marks)". Decide also whether the v2.0 share is replaced or kept (F3).
6. **Tags** on AnkiWeb, e.g. `lithuanian lietuvių a1 vocabulary pictures audio`.
